survivingClaim: The Riemann-Siegel half-sum F_N(s) = sum_{n<=N} n^(-s), N = floor(sqrt(t/2 pi)), is not in Hermite-Biehler position in any tested matched window: it has zeros in Re s > 1/2 at about one per five zeros of Z (ratio 0.17 at 1e4 to 0.215 at 1e12; referee recount 0.19 at 3e7). The arb-certified counts 5372, 7260, 8835 in windows of length 1e4 at 1e8, 1e10, 1e12 are rigorous lower bounds for the number of right zeros (disjoint certified squares); absence of further zeros rests on float64 winding counts. Smooth cut-off and unequal lengths do not remove the zeros. DH, chi_5, translate, period-3 and random-sign controls also fail; DH is slightly nearer to passing than zeta. The size of the failure does depend on multiplicativity (Bohr random-multiplicative model reproduces the zeta/chi_5 excess and the DH deficit), in the adverse direction, so the stated reason "second moments of |a_n| only" does not survive. By the Siegel/Levinson identity (E3) the family is the unmollified Levinson method with loss equal to the right-zero count. Positive density at matched height is measured/certified in finite windows at six heights, not proved for all heights. No statement about zeros of zeta.

lesson: Any splitting Z = 2 Re f with f a Dirichlet polynomial in the theta frame depends on |a_n| and the functional equation only: by a Gaussian second-moment model the negative-phase fraction is (1-r)/2 with r = c1/sqrt(c0 c2) < 1 (Cauchy-Schwarz), about 6.7% for the sharp cutoff. Multiplicativity never enters; the functional equation only confines the right zeros to within about 2/log N of the line. Close pairs of Z zeros (7 of 8 tested, including Lehmer 7005) carry a right zero of F_N nearby.
